title: Account deletion route lacks direct regression coverage
reasoning: The reviewed feature exposes a destructive account-deletion endpoint, but the included tests cover unrelated scraping, Bible text retrieval, devotionals, email behavior, fast views, and admin icon actions. There is no first-class test evidence for the route resolving to DeleteAccountView, requiring authentication, rejecting unsafe methods or unauthenticated callers, or deleting only the requesting user's account data. Because this route crosses auth and data-loss trust boundaries, regressions could remove accounts incorrectly or make deletion unreachable without being caught by the shown suite.
recommendation: Add focused tests for /hub/account/delete/ that exercise URL resolution and the intended HTTP contract, including authenticated success, unauthenticated rejection, allowed methods, CSRF/auth expectations if applicable, and verification that only the current user's account-owned data is deleted.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test files do not reference account/delete, DeleteAccountView, account deletion, or user deletion behavior; their headers and classes show coverage for other features instead.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create hub/tests/test_account_delete.py with API client tests for the account-delete route covering authenticated deletion, unauthenticated denial, method handling, and isolation from other users' data.
minimumFixScope: Add route-level and view-level tests for DeleteAccountView; update the view only if those tests reveal an auth, method, or deletion-scope defect.
